findings.evidence: mathlib/.github/workflows/release_cache.yml:51-79 — `gate` checks `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/master` and the `build` job runs only `if: needs.gate.outputs.off_master == 'true'`; a skipped job leaves the run's conclusion `success`. resolve_deps.py:171-173 filters only on `status == "completed" and .conclusion == "success"` plus `head_branch == tag`.
findings.fix: Apply the release_cache branch only when the tag commit is off master, e.g. gate it on `self.src.compare(repo, sha, 'master')[0] not in ('ahead', 'identical')`, or verify the run's `build` job actually ran rather than trusting the run conclusion. Add a test for an on-master tag whose master-push build has not succeeded.
findings.issue: `cache_published` accepts any successful `release_cache.yml` run on the tag, but mathlib's `release_cache.yml` has a `gate` job that sets `off_master=false` and skips the build for tags that point at a master commit; such a run still concludes `success`. So for an on-master tag (`.0` releases and plain rcs — exactly the tags Physlib bumps to) whose master-push `build.yml` run has not finished yet, the resolver reports the cache as published and offers that M, which is the failure mode `check-bump.sh` step 2b was written to prevent ("a very fresh tip can carry a green bors status while its cache is still hours away", scripts/check-bump.sh:157-162). The module docstring and docs/dependency-bumps.md both state the rule with the "off master" qualifier; the code omits it.

summary: No new Lean mathematics to assess; the only Lean change is About-page prose that matches the repo's actual dependency setup. One documented invariant is not implemented: the cache gate accepts a `release_cache.yml` run that mathlib's own workflow skips, so an uncached mathlib commit can be offered.
